speeds.instant: under a second, on every keystroke or save
speeds.seconds: seconds, on every save or change
speeds.minutes: minutes, before a commit or merge
speeds.hours: hours, nightly or in the background
speeds.continuous: always on, in production or as a long-running job

tiers.edit: fires while the agent edits (editor, compiler, watch mode)
tiers.inner: the agent's change loop, run after every change
tiers.gate: the one-command gate before a commit, merge or release

groups.static: Static signals: catch bugs without running the code
groups.examples: Tests by scope: examples written by hand
groups.generated: Generated and oracle-free tests: more inputs than anyone would write
groups.runtime: Runtime checks: memory, concurrency, performance and resilience

bug_classes.edge: edge cases: empty, huge, unicode, negative, boundary values
bug_classes.types: null, undefined, wrong shape, wrong type
bug_classes.wiring: components wired wrong, config, dependency injection, routes
bug_classes.contract: API or schema breaks between services, clients or versions
bug_classes.ui: broken flows, wrong UI state, dead buttons
bug_classes.platform: works on one OS, browser, device or locale only
bug_classes.resilience: bad behaviour when dependencies fail or slow down
bug_classes.requirements: built the wrong thing, confusing UX
bug_classes.regression: something that used to work broke

techniques.name: Strict type checking
techniques.what: The compiler or checker proves shapes, nullability and call signatures before anything runs.
techniques.strengths: Instant, exhaustive over all paths, points at file and line, and makes refactors safe for agents.
techniques.gaps: Says nothing about values, logic or behaviour, and escape hatches (any, force unwraps, casts) silently switch it off.
techniques.signal: Best-in-class: fastest, deterministic, exact location, readable message.
techniques.use_when: Always. Turn on the strictest mode the language offers and ban escape hatches in new code.

techniques.name: Linting and static analysis
techniques.what: Rules flag bug patterns, unsafe APIs, dead code and style drift.
techniques.strengths: Encodes past mistakes as rules, runs in milliseconds, and gives agents a precise fix hint.
techniques.gaps: Pattern-based, so it misses novel bugs, and noisy rule sets train agents to suppress warnings.
techniques.signal: Excellent when the rule set is curated and warnings fail the build.
techniques.use_when: Always. Turn each escaped bug class that a pattern can catch into a custom rule.

techniques.name: Assertions and design by contract
techniques.what: Preconditions, postconditions and invariants checked inside the code at runtime.
techniques.strengths: Turns silent corruption into a loud failure at the point of the bug, and makes every other test stronger.
techniques.gaps: Only fires on paths that run, and costs a little at runtime.
techniques.signal: Fails exactly where state first goes wrong instead of three calls later.
techniques.use_when: Core data structures, state machines, money, anything with an invariant you can state.

techniques.name: Schema validation at boundaries
techniques.what: Parse every external input (HTTP, files, env, LLM output) against a schema before using it.
techniques.strengths: Extends type safety to data the compiler can't see, with clear errors at the edge.
techniques.gaps: Validates shape, not meaning, and schemas drift if they aren't the single source of truth.
techniques.signal: Names the exact field that is wrong.
techniques.use_when: Any input crossing a process, network or trust boundary.

tools.jvm: Jackson with strict mode, JSON Schema

techniques.name: Security static analysis (SAST)
techniques.what: Scans source for injection, unsafe deserialization, weak crypto and taint flows.
techniques.strengths: Runs before deploy and finds whole classes of vulnerability across the codebase.
techniques.gaps: False positives, and blind to runtime configuration and business-logic flaws.
techniques.signal: Good location, noisy unless rules are tuned.
techniques.use_when: Anything handling user input, auth or money.

techniques.name: Unit tests
techniques.what: One function, class or module checked on hand-picked examples.
techniques.strengths: Fast, precise failure location, cheap to write, and the main inner-loop signal for agents.
techniques.gaps: Only covers cases someone thought of, and heavy mocking tests the mocks instead of the code.
techniques.signal: Excellent when tests hit public behaviour and failure messages show expected against actual.
techniques.use_when: Pure logic, parsers, formatters, calculations, state transitions.

techniques.name: Parameterized and table-driven tests
techniques.what: One test body run over many rows of inputs and expected outputs.
techniques.strengths: Cheap breadth, and each escaped bug becomes one new row.
techniques.gaps: Still limited to the rows written down.
techniques.signal: Names the failing row.
techniques.use_when: Any function with a clear input-to-output mapping.

techniques.name: Component tests
techniques.what: A larger unit, such as a UI component or service module, exercised through its public interface.
techniques.strengths: Realistic behaviour without booting the whole system.
techniques.gaps: Fakes at the edges can drift from reality.
techniques.signal: Good, as long as queries target roles and labels rather than internals.
techniques.use_when: UI components with state, modules with several collaborators.

techniques.name: Integration tests
techniques.what: Real components together: code plus a real database, queue, filesystem or HTTP server.
techniques.strengths: Catches serialization, query, schema and configuration bugs that mocks hide.
techniques.gaps: Slower, needs setup, and failures point at a seam rather than a line.
techniques.signal: Good when each test owns its data and logs the failing request.
techniques.use_when: Anything that talks to storage or another process.

techniques.name: Contract tests
techniques.what: Provider and consumer each verify they honour a shared API contract.
techniques.strengths: Catches breaking API changes in seconds without a full environment.
techniques.gaps: Only as good as the contract, and blind to business logic.
techniques.signal: Names the field or endpoint that broke.
techniques.use_when: Separately deployed services, mobile apps against a backend, public APIs.

tools.any: Pact, Schemathesis for OpenAPI, buf breaking for protobuf

techniques.name: End-to-end tests
techniques.what: Real user flows driven through the UI against the running stack.
techniques.strengths: Closest to what users experience, and proves the whole path works.
techniques.gaps: Slow, flaky, costly to maintain, and failures point at a screen rather than a cause.
techniques.signal: Weak alone: pair with traces, screenshots and logs so the agent sees why.
techniques.use_when: A handful of revenue-critical or signup-critical paths only.

techniques.name: Smoke tests
techniques.what: The build starts, the main page loads, the health endpoint answers.
techniques.strengths: Seconds to run, and catches the broken build before anything else does.
techniques.gaps: Shallow by design.
techniques.signal: Binary and fast.
techniques.use_when: After every build and every deploy.

tools.any: curl script, one Playwright test, app launch check

techniques.name: Acceptance tests
techniques.what: Checks the software meets the stated requirement, often written as Given/When/Then.
techniques.strengths: Ties tests to the reason the feature exists, and gives agents an executable spec.
techniques.gaps: Late and often manual, and only as precise as the requirement.
techniques.signal: Good as a definition of done for an agent task.
techniques.use_when: Before starting a feature: write the acceptance check first.

tools.any: Cucumber, behave, plain tests named as scenarios

techniques.name: Property-based tests
techniques.what: Generate many inputs and assert invariants such as round-trips, ordering and idempotence.
techniques.strengths: Finds cases nobody imagined, and shrinks each failure to a minimal reproduction.
techniques.gaps: Properties take thought to write, and rare paths can still be missed.
techniques.signal: Excellent: the shrunk counterexample is the bug report.
techniques.use_when: Parsers, serializers, encoders, math, data structures, anything with a round-trip.

techniques.name: Model-based and stateful tests
techniques.what: Random sequences of operations run against the system and a simple model, compared step by step.
techniques.strengths: Finds the bug that needs five specific steps in order.
techniques.gaps: The model is real work and can share the system's misunderstanding.
techniques.signal: Shrinks to the shortest failing operation sequence.
techniques.use_when: Caches, editors, sync engines, state machines, anything with history.

techniques.name: Property-based UI exploration
techniques.what: A tool drives the real UI with generated clicks, typing, scrolling and navigation, and checks temporal properties (always, eventually within, next) on every state it reaches, including leak properties over DOM nodes, listeners and heap.
techniques.strengths: Turns every design, product and accessibility rule into a check on every reachable screen, finds the bug that needs a dozen steps in an unplanned order, and shrinks the failing trace with a screenshot of each state.
techniques.gaps: Random exploration only reaches shallow states unless runs are long, seeded with realistic data and steered with weighted actions; replay is not deterministic outside a deterministic hypervisor; a property never seen to fail may be checking nothing.
techniques.signal: Good when every violation is shrunk and carries its trace, screenshots and the property name; poor when browser driver errors are counted as failures.
techniques.use_when: Any web or terminal UI an agent edits often: forms, checkout, dashboards, multi-step flows. A short run at the gate, long swarm fuzz campaigns nightly.

techniques.name: Fuzzing
techniques.what: Coverage-guided mutation of inputs, looking for crashes, hangs and sanitizer failures.
techniques.strengths: Finds memory bugs, parser holes and security issues that nothing else does.
techniques.gaps: Mostly finds crashes rather than wrong answers, and needs CPU time and a harness.
techniques.signal: Saves a crashing input that becomes a permanent regression test.
techniques.use_when: Untrusted input: file formats, network protocols, parsers, decoders.

techniques.name: Metamorphic tests
techniques.what: Assert relations between outputs when there is no exact expected answer.
techniques.strengths: Works for search, ML, simulations and compilers where no oracle exists.
techniques.gaps: Good relations are hard to find, and they only check part of correctness.
techniques.signal: Clear when a relation breaks, but the root cause needs digging.
techniques.use_when: Ranking, search, recommendations, numerical code, LLM pipelines.

techniques.name: Differential tests
techniques.what: Run two implementations or two versions on the same inputs and compare outputs.
techniques.strengths: Needs no oracle, and is perfect for rewrites, ports and optimisations.
techniques.gaps: Both sides can share a bug.
techniques.signal: Shows the input and both outputs.
techniques.use_when: Refactors, rewrites, ports to a new language, fast paths against slow reference code.

tools.any: a property test that calls both implementations

techniques.name: Snapshot and characterization tests
techniques.what: Compare output to a stored known-good copy.
techniques.strengths: Near-zero effort, and locks down legacy behaviour before a refactor.
techniques.gaps: Locks in bugs too, and agents and humans rubber-stamp snapshot updates.
techniques.signal: Shows a diff, but cannot say whether the change was intended.
techniques.use_when: Before refactoring legacy code, for CLI output, generated code, serialized formats.

techniques.name: Boundary value and equivalence partitioning
techniques.what: Pick inputs at the edges and one from each class of the input space.
techniques.strengths: Cheap, and targets where off-by-one bugs live.
techniques.gaps: Depends on finding the right boundaries.
techniques.signal: Precise.
techniques.use_when: Ranges, limits, pagination, dates, money, string lengths.

techniques.name: Combinatorial and pairwise tests
techniques.what: Cover every pair of configuration values instead of every combination.
techniques.strengths: Shrinks large configuration matrices to a handful of runs.
techniques.gaps: Misses bugs that need three or more factors at once.
techniques.signal: Names the failing combination.
techniques.use_when: Feature flags, settings screens, build matrices, option-heavy CLIs.

techniques.name: Sanitizers
techniques.what: Instrumented builds that trap memory errors, undefined behaviour and data races as they happen.
techniques.strengths: Turns silent corruption into a stack trace at the faulting line.
techniques.gaps: Only checks paths the tests run, and slows the build by about two to three times.
techniques.signal: Excellent: exact stack and access type.
techniques.use_when: Any native, unsafe or concurrent code. Run the existing suite under them.

techniques.name: Concurrency and interleaving tests
techniques.what: Explore thread and task interleavings systematically or under stress.
techniques.strengths: Reproduces races that normal runs hit once a month.
techniques.gaps: Can't cover the whole interleaving space.
techniques.signal: Good when the tool replays the failing schedule.
techniques.use_when: Shared mutable state, actors, locks, async pipelines, lock-free code.

techniques.name: Deterministic simulation
techniques.what: Run the whole system on a fake clock, network and disk with a seeded scheduler, injecting faults.
techniques.strengths: Every failure replays exactly from its seed, which agents can debug step by step.
techniques.gaps: Requires designing the system for injectable time, I/O and randomness.
techniques.signal: Best possible for distributed bugs: one seed reproduces the failure.
techniques.use_when: Databases, sync engines, distributed systems, anything with retries and timeouts.

techniques.name: Benchmarks and performance regression tests
techniques.what: Measure latency, throughput, allocations or frame time of hot paths and compare to a baseline.
techniques.strengths: Catches the slow commit when it lands, not when users complain.
techniques.gaps: Noisy on shared machines, and needs a stable baseline.
techniques.signal: Report the number and the change, and fail only on a large, repeated regression.
techniques.use_when: Hot loops, startup time, rendering, audio, anything users feel.

techniques.name: Load, stress, spike and soak tests
techniques.what: Drive expected, extreme, sudden or sustained traffic and watch latency, errors and memory.
techniques.strengths: Shows capacity, breaking points, leaks and autoscaling behaviour.
techniques.gaps: Synthetic traffic differs from real traffic, and environments cost money.
techniques.signal: Coarse: tells you that it broke, and traces tell you why.
techniques.use_when: Before launches, pricing changes or anything expecting a traffic jump.

techniques.name: Chaos and fault injection
techniques.what: Kill processes, drop packets, add latency and fail dependencies on purpose.
techniques.strengths: Proves retries, timeouts and fallbacks actually work.
techniques.gaps: Risky without good observability, and needs a production-like environment.
techniques.signal: Useful only with traces and alerts in place.
techniques.use_when: Services with dependencies, offline-capable apps, payment flows.

tools.any: Toxiproxy, Chaos Mesh, network link conditioner

techniques.name: Visual regression tests
techniques.what: Screenshot pages or components and diff them against approved baselines.
techniques.strengths: Catches CSS and layout breakage that functional tests pass straight through.
techniques.gaps: Font and anti-aliasing noise, and someone must review each diff.
techniques.signal: The diff image is direct evidence an agent can read.
techniques.use_when: Design systems, marketing pages, any UI an agent edits often.

techniques.name: Accessibility checks
techniques.what: Automated audits for roles, labels, contrast and focus, plus manual screen reader passes.
techniques.strengths: Automated rules catch a solid share of issues for almost no effort.
techniques.gaps: Automation misses most real usability problems for disabled users.
techniques.signal: Precise rule, element and fix.
techniques.use_when: Every user interface.

techniques.name: Compatibility and cross-platform tests
techniques.what: Run the suite across browsers, OS versions, devices, runtimes and screen sizes.
techniques.strengths: Catches the bug that only exists on Safari, Linux or an older OS.
techniques.gaps: The matrix explodes, and device farms cost money.
techniques.signal: Names the platform.
techniques.use_when: Shipping to several browsers, OS versions or devices.

techniques.name: Localization and pseudo-localization
techniques.what: Run the UI with long, accented, right-to-left text and other locales' formats.
techniques.strengths: Finds truncation, hard-coded strings and date or number format bugs early.
techniques.gaps: Needs native speakers to judge translation quality.
techniques.signal: Visible in screenshots.
techniques.use_when: Any app with, or planning, translations.

techniques.name: Exploratory testing
techniques.what: A person or an agent drives the real product freely, looking for anything wrong.
techniques.strengths: Finds what nobody thought to script, and agents can now do a useful first pass.
techniques.gaps: Not repeatable unless findings become tests.
techniques.signal: Rich but unstructured: turn each finding into an automated test.
techniques.use_when: After any user-visible change, before a release.

tools.any: agent browser or simulator control, session recording

techniques.name: Usability testing
techniques.what: Real users attempt real tasks while you watch.
techniques.strengths: Finds confusion that no assertion can.
techniques.gaps: Slow, small samples, subjective.
techniques.signal: Qualitative.
techniques.use_when: New flows, onboarding, anything with drop-off.

techniques.name: Dependency and secret scanning
techniques.what: Check dependencies against vulnerability databases and the repo for committed secrets.
techniques.strengths: Automatic and cheap, and catches the leaked key before it ships.
techniques.gaps: Only known CVEs, and noisy about unreachable code.
techniques.signal: Names the package, version and fix.
techniques.use_when: Every repo.

techniques.name: Dynamic security scanning (DAST)
techniques.what: Attack the running app with known exploit patterns.
techniques.strengths: Finds issues that are actually exploitable in the deployed configuration.
techniques.gaps: Limited reach into authenticated or deep flows.
techniques.signal: Names the URL and payload.
techniques.use_when: Public web apps and APIs.

techniques.name: Penetration testing
techniques.what: Skilled attackers probe the system by hand.
techniques.strengths: Finds logic and authorization flaws that tools miss.
techniques.gaps: Expensive, a point-in-time snapshot, and only as good as the tester.
techniques.signal: Rich report, slow.
techniques.use_when: Before handling money, health data or enterprise customers.

techniques.name: Code coverage
techniques.what: Measure which lines and branches the tests execute.
techniques.strengths: Cheap, and shows code no test even runs.
techniques.gaps: Executed is not checked: high coverage with weak assertions proves little, and the number is easy to game.
techniques.signal: A map of untested code, not a quality score.
techniques.use_when: Finding untested risky code. Read it on the diff, not as a repo-wide floor.

techniques.name: Mutation testing
techniques.what: Inject small bugs into the code and check that some test fails for each one.
techniques.strengths: The honest measure of whether tests check anything, and it names the exact unchecked line.
techniques.gaps: Slow on large code, and equivalent mutants add noise.
techniques.signal: Each surviving mutant is a concrete missing assertion.
techniques.use_when: On the riskiest modules, or only on the lines a change touched.

techniques.name: Flaky test detection
techniques.what: Rerun tests many times, in random order and in parallel, to find nondeterminism.
techniques.strengths: Restores trust in the signal, which agents need more than humans do.
techniques.gaps: Finds the flake but not its cause.
techniques.signal: A flaky test is a lying signal: fix it or quarantine it.
techniques.use_when: As soon as any test has failed and then passed on retry.

techniques.name: Model checking
techniques.what: Exhaustively explore every state of a design written as a formal spec.
techniques.strengths: Finds design bugs in protocols and concurrency before any code exists.
techniques.gaps: Checks the model, not the code, and large state spaces blow up.
techniques.signal: Gives the exact counterexample trace.
techniques.use_when: Protocols, distributed algorithms, locking schemes, sync logic.

techniques.name: Formal verification
techniques.what: Machine-checked proofs that code meets a specification for every input.
techniques.strengths: A guarantee rather than a sample.
techniques.gaps: Expensive, and proves the spec, which can itself be wrong.
techniques.signal: Agents are getting good at closing proof obligations, which changes the cost.
techniques.use_when: Crypto, consensus, compilers, safety-critical kernels.

techniques.name: Symbolic and concolic execution
techniques.what: Solve for inputs that reach each path through the code.
techniques.strengths: Reaches deep branches guarded by exact values that random inputs never hit.
techniques.gaps: Path explosion on large programs.
techniques.signal: Produces a concrete failing input.
techniques.use_when: Small, critical functions with complex branching.

techniques.name: Canary and progressive rollout
techniques.what: Release to a small share of users, compare health metrics, then widen.
techniques.strengths: Real users and real data with a small blast radius.
techniques.gaps: Some users still hit the bug, and it needs good metrics.
techniques.signal: Fast when error rates are wired to automatic rollback.
techniques.use_when: Any service with enough traffic to compare.

tools.any: feature flags, staged rollouts, TestFlight, Play staged rollout

techniques.name: Shadow traffic and replay
techniques.what: Send copies of real requests to the new version and compare responses without serving them.
techniques.strengths: Production realism with no user impact.
techniques.gaps: Side effects are tricky, and it doubles the infrastructure.
techniques.signal: Shows the request and both responses.
techniques.use_when: Rewrites of request-handling services.

tools.any: GoReplay, mirrored traffic in the proxy

techniques.name: Synthetic monitoring
techniques.what: Scripted checks run against production on a schedule.
techniques.strengths: Catches outages and broken deploys before users report them.
techniques.gaps: Only covers the scripted paths.
techniques.signal: Fast and binary.
techniques.use_when: Signup, checkout, login and health endpoints.

tools.any: Checkly, a scheduled Playwright or curl job

techniques.name: Observability and error tracking
techniques.what: Structured logs, traces, metrics and crash reports from real use.
techniques.strengths: Catches what no pre-production environment reproduces, with real stack traces.
techniques.gaps: Users meet the bug first.
techniques.signal: Feed every new production error back as a failing test.
techniques.use_when: Every shipped product.

techniques.name: A/B and beta testing
techniques.what: Compare variants on live users, or ship early builds to a willing group.
techniques.strengths: Measures real behaviour and real-world environments.
techniques.gaps: Tests outcomes, not correctness, and needs traffic or testers.
techniques.signal: Slow, statistical.
techniques.use_when: Product decisions, pricing, onboarding.

techniques.name: LLM evals
techniques.what: Score model or agent output on a fixed dataset with code checks, rubrics or model graders.
techniques.strengths: The only way to know whether a prompt or model change made an AI feature better or worse.
techniques.gaps: Graders can be wrong, datasets go stale, and scores are noisy.
techniques.signal: Report the per-case diff, not just the average.
techniques.use_when: Any feature whose output comes from a model.

tools.any: promptfoo, Inspect, Braintrust, plain pytest with fixtures

techniques.name: Code review
techniques.what: A human or a second model reads the change.
techniques.strengths: Catches design problems, wrong assumptions and missing tests.
techniques.gaps: Inconsistent and tiring, and it misses subtle bugs.
techniques.signal: Strongest when the reviewer is a different model or person than the author.
techniques.use_when: Every change worth keeping.
